hlni.insight: Degree labels like B.Com or BBA hide the actual assessment criteria of a course.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles represent the entire learning experience.
hlni.viewerChange: Students start auditing syllabi for assessment methods instead of relying on generic degree labels.
hlni.support: Auditing specific assessment criteria provides granular data that degree titles cannot offer.
hlni.payoff: The viewer moves from confusion to asking a concrete, actionable question about grading.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: The Hidden Criteria Hunt
creativeAngle: Auditing syllabus grading labels to find actionable questions
objective: Teach students to look past degree titles to specific assessment methods
targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Vague Syllabus
shots.visual: A student points at a laptop screen showing a mock course syllabus with an empty bracketed field.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA feels like guessing. Look at this.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close up on the screen, shaky cam for trendy feel.

shots.name: The Audit Method
shots.visual: Student uses a digital marker to circle 'Grading: [Hidden]' on the screen.
shots.dialogue: Stop guessing. Audit the criteria. Ask what work you produce and how it gets graded.
shots.cameraPerformance: Quick cuts between the screen and the student's face.

shots.name: The Targeted Question
shots.visual: Student types a question into a notes app on their phone.
shots.dialogue: Don't pick a title. Ask: How is the final grade calculated for this specific project?
shots.onscreenText: How is the final grade calculated for this specific project?
shots.cameraPerformance: Focus on the phone screen showing the typed question.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Transforming passive degree comparison into an active search for assessment transparency.
shootingPriority: Close up of student typing question

selected.title: The Hidden Criteria Hunt
selected.audienceGap: Students treat course selection as a mystery instead of a searchable inquiry.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Turns curiosity into a structured search for assessment criteria.
selected.concept: A 'hunt' for hidden grading criteria within a mock course syllabus screen.
selected.device: A digital cursor highlighting specific missing grading tags on a screen.
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: A mock course syllabus page with missing evaluation details.
demonstration.observation: The viewer discovers that the grading method is obscured by generic labels.
demonstration.nextQuestion: How is the final grade calculated for this specific project?

comparedWith.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
comparedWith.device: A graphic overlay displays a 'Decision Tree' that dead-ends at 'Insufficient Evidence'.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: Direct-to-camera conversation followed by a quick close-up of a 'Sticking Point' logbook.
